**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters") in the [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") drama series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_ (2007–2015), and [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") fantasy series _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3)

In addition to supporting roles in films such as _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, and _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_ (2023), and _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_ (2024), among others.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking [ballroom dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballroom_dancing "Ballroom dancing") classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2000–2017: Beginnings and Mad Men")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_(cropped_2).jpg)

Shipka at the 2010 [Screen Actors Guild Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards "Screen Actors Guild Awards")

In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters"), the daughter of main character [Don Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Draper "Don Draper"), on the 2007–2015 TV series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in [season four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_4) "Mad Men (season 4)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series") in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _[Austin American-Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin\_American-Statesman "Austin American-Statesman")_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actress_in_a_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series"), writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in [season three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_3) "Mad Men (season 3)"), this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-roe-12)

Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced [Jinora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender_characters#Jinora "List of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters") in the [Nickelodeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon "Nickelodeon") animated series _[The Legend of Korra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Korra "The Legend of Korra")_, the sequel to _[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:\_The\_Last\_Airbender "Avatar: The Last Airbender")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Magazine "Time Magazine").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-14) That same year, [IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire") included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") movie _[Flowers in the Attic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers\_in\_the\_Attic\_(2014\_film) "Flowers in the Attic (2014 film)")_, based on the [1979 novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_in_the_Attic "Flowers in the Attic") by [V. C. Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._C._Andrews "V. C. Andrews").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with [Emma Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Roberts "Emma Roberts") in the [Osgood Perkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_Perkins "Oz Perkins") horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet") in the fantasy thriller _[One & Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_&\_Two "One & Two")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of [Studio Ghibli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli "Studio Ghibli")'s _[When Marnie Was There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_Marnie\_Was\_There\_(film) "When Marnie Was There (film)")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed [B.D. Hyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.D._Hyman "B.D. Hyman"), daughter of [Bette Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bette_Davis "Bette Davis"), in the [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") television series _[Feud: Bette and Joan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud\_(American\_TV\_series) "Feud (American TV series)")_.

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Chilling Adventures of Sabrina")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png)

Shipka in 2018.

In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ series based on the [comic series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)

Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite [Stanley Tucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Tucci "Stanley Tucci") in [John R. Leonetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Leonetti "John R. Leonetti")'s [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(2019\_film) "The Silence (2019 film)")_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by [Tim Lebbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Lebbon "Tim Lebbon").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_film "Christmas film")[romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") film _[Let It Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow\_(2019\_film) "Let It Snow (2019 film)")_, based on the novel _[Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow:\_Three\_Holiday\_Romances "Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2022–present: Further work")]

In 2022, Shipka starred alongside [Diane Kruger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Kruger "Diane Kruger") in the psychological drama series _[Swimming with Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming\_with\_Sharks\_(TV\_series) "Swimming with Sharks (TV series)")_, inspired by the [1994 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_with_Sharks "Swimming with Sharks").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _[Wildflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildflower\_(2022\_film) "Wildflower (2022 film)")_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") political drama limited series [_White House Plumbers_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Plumbers_(miniseries) "White House Plumbers (miniseries)"), portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of [E. Howard Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._Howard_Hunt "E. Howard Hunt").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress [Olivia Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Holt "Olivia Holt") in [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video")'s 1980s horror-comedy _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ and _[Red One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_One\_(film) "Red One (film)")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside [Nico Hiraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Hiraga "Nico Hiraga") in the [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") romantic comedy _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _[Stone Cold Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone\_Cold\_Fox "Stone Cold Fox")_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)

In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") drama _[Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry\_(TV\_series) "Industry (TV series)")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _[Idiots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiots\_(2026\_film) "Idiots (2026 film)")_, which premiered at the [2026 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Sundance_Film_Festival "2026 Sundance Film Festival").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)

She is set to star alongside [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") in the romantic comedy _[Goodbye Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye\_Girl\_(film) "Goodbye Girl (film)")_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with [Mckenna Grace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mckenna_Grace "Mckenna Grace"), who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters") in the [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") drama series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_ (2007–2015), and [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") fantasy series _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3)

In addition to supporting roles in films such as _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, and _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_ (2023), and _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_ (2024), among others.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking [ballroom dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballroom_dancing "Ballroom dancing") classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2000–2017: Beginnings and Mad Men")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_(cropped_2).jpg)

Shipka at the 2010 [Screen Actors Guild Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards "Screen Actors Guild Awards")

In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters"), the daughter of main character [Don Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Draper "Don Draper"), on the 2007–2015 TV series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in [season four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_4) "Mad Men (season 4)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series") in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _[Austin American-Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin\_American-Statesman "Austin American-Statesman")_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actress_in_a_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series"), writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in [season three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_3) "Mad Men (season 3)"), this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-roe-12)

Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced [Jinora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender_characters#Jinora "List of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters") in the [Nickelodeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon "Nickelodeon") animated series _[The Legend of Korra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Korra "The Legend of Korra")_, the sequel to _[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:\_The\_Last\_Airbender "Avatar: The Last Airbender")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Magazine "Time Magazine").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-14) That same year, [IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire") included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") movie _[Flowers in the Attic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers\_in\_the\_Attic\_(2014\_film) "Flowers in the Attic (2014 film)")_, based on the [1979 novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_in_the_Attic "Flowers in the Attic") by [V. C. Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._C._Andrews "V. C. Andrews").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with [Emma Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Roberts "Emma Roberts") in the [Osgood Perkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_Perkins "Oz Perkins") horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet") in the fantasy thriller _[One & Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_&\_Two "One & Two")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of [Studio Ghibli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli "Studio Ghibli")'s _[When Marnie Was There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_Marnie\_Was\_There\_(film) "When Marnie Was There (film)")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed [B.D. Hyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.D._Hyman "B.D. ### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Chilling Adventures of Sabrina")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png)

Shipka in 2018.

In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ series based on the [comic series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-23)

Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite [Stanley Tucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Tucci "Stanley Tucci") in [John R. Leonetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Leonetti "John R. Leonetti")'s [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(2019\_film) "The Silence (2019 film)")_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by [Tim Lebbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Lebbon "Tim Lebbon").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-25) Shipka learned [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_film "Christmas film")[romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") film _[Let It Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow\_(2019\_film) "Let It Snow (2019 film)")_, based on the novel _[Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow:\_Three\_Holiday\_Romances "Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-27)

Howard Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._Howard_Hunt "E. Howard Hunt").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress [Olivia Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Holt "Olivia Holt") in [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video")'s 1980s horror-comedy _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ and _[Red One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_One\_(film) "Red One (film)")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside [Nico Hiraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Hiraga "Nico Hiraga") in the [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") romantic comedy _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _[Stone Cold Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone\_Cold\_Fox "Stone Cold Fox")_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-38)

In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") drama _[Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry\_(TV\_series) "Industry (TV series)")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _[Idiots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiots\_(2026\_film) "Idiots (2026 film)")_, which premiered at the [2026 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Sundance_Film_Festival "2026 Sundance Film Festival").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-41)

She is set to star alongside [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") in the romantic comedy _[Goodbye Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye\_Girl\_(film) "Goodbye Girl (film)")_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with [Mckenna Grace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mckenna_Grace "Mckenna Grace"), who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiernan_Shipka#cite_note-43)

**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters") in the [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") drama series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_ (2007–2015), and [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") fantasy series _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-deadline-3)

In addition to supporting roles in films such as _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, and _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_ (2023), and _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_ (2024), among others.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking [ballroom dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballroom_dancing "Ballroom dancing") classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2000–2017: Beginnings and Mad Men")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_(cropped_2).jpg)

Shipka at the 2010 [Screen Actors Guild Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards "Screen Actors Guild Awards")

In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters"), the daughter of main character [Don Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Draper "Don Draper"), on the 2007–2015 TV series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in [season four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_4) "Mad Men (season 4)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series") in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _[Austin American-Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin\_American-Statesman "Austin American-Statesman")_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actress_in_a_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series"), writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in [season three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_3) "Mad Men (season 3)"), this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-roe-12)

Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced [Jinora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender_characters#Jinora "List of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters") in the [Nickelodeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon "Nickelodeon") animated series _[The Legend of Korra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Korra "The Legend of Korra")_, the sequel to _[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:\_The\_Last\_Airbender "Avatar: The Last Airbender")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Magazine "Time Magazine").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-14) That same year, [IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire") included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") movie _[Flowers in the Attic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers\_in\_the\_Attic\_(2014\_film) "Flowers in the Attic (2014 film)")_, based on the [1979 novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_in_the_Attic "Flowers in the Attic") by [V. C. Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._C._Andrews "V. C. Andrews").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with [Emma Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Roberts "Emma Roberts") in the [Osgood Perkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_Perkins "Oz Perkins") horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet") in the fantasy thriller _[One & Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_&\_Two "One & Two")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of [Studio Ghibli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli "Studio Ghibli")'s _[When Marnie Was There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_Marnie\_Was\_There\_(film) "When Marnie Was There (film)")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed [B.D. Hyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.D._Hyman "B.D. Hyman"), daughter of [Bette Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bette_Davis "Bette Davis"), in the [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") television series _[Feud: Bette and Joan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud\_(American\_TV\_series) "Feud (American TV series)")_.

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Chilling Adventures of Sabrina")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png)

Shipka in 2018.

In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ series based on the [comic series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-23)

Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite [Stanley Tucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Tucci "Stanley Tucci") in [John R. Leonetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Leonetti "John R. Leonetti")'s [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(2019\_film) "The Silence (2019 film)")_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by [Tim Lebbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Lebbon "Tim Lebbon").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-25) Shipka learned [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_film "Christmas film")[romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") film _[Let It Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow\_(2019\_film) "Let It Snow (2019 film)")_, based on the novel _[Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow:\_Three\_Holiday\_Romances "Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2022–present: Further work")]

In 2022, Shipka starred alongside [Diane Kruger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Kruger "Diane Kruger") in the psychological drama series _[Swimming with Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming\_with\_Sharks\_(TV\_series) "Swimming with Sharks (TV series)")_, inspired by the [1994 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_with_Sharks "Swimming with Sharks").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _[Wildflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildflower\_(2022\_film) "Wildflower (2022 film)")_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") political drama limited series [_White House Plumbers_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Plumbers_(miniseries) "White House Plumbers (miniseries)"), portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of [E. Howard Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._Howard_Hunt "E. Howard Hunt").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress [Olivia Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Holt "Olivia Holt") in [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video")'s 1980s horror-comedy _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ and _[Red One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_One\_(film) "Red One (film)")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside [Nico Hiraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Hiraga "Nico Hiraga") in the [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") romantic comedy _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _[Stone Cold Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone\_Cold\_Fox "Stone Cold Fox")_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-38)

In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") drama _[Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry\_(TV\_series) "Industry (TV series)")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _[Idiots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiots\_(2026\_film) "Idiots (2026 film)")_, which premiered at the [2026 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Sundance_Film_Festival "2026 Sundance Film Festival").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-41)

She is set to star alongside [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") in the romantic comedy _[Goodbye Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye\_Girl\_(film) "Goodbye Girl (film)")_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with [Mckenna Grace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mckenna_Grace "Mckenna Grace"), who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-43)

**Kiernan Brennan Shipka** (born November 10, 1999)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-chicago_tribune-2) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters") in the [AMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)") drama series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_ (2007–2015), and [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") fantasy series _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ (2018–2020) and the sixth season of [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_ (2021–2022).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-deadline-3)

In addition to supporting roles in films such as _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, and _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_ (2015), _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_ (2023), and _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_ (2024), among others.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-MadTween-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-6) She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-7) She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking [ballroom dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballroom_dancing "Ballroom dancing") classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-8) When she was six, her family relocated to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to help with her acting career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2000–2017: Beginnings and _Mad Men_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2000–2017: Beginnings and Mad Men")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_%28cropped_2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_(cropped_2).jpg)

Shipka at the 2010 [Screen Actors Guild Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards "Screen Actors Guild Awards")

In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-dazeddigital-9) She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-MadTween-4) After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as [Sally Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mad_Men_characters#Sally_Draper "List of Mad Men characters"), the daughter of main character [Don Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Draper "Don Draper"), on the 2007–2015 TV series _[Mad Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Men "Mad Men")_. She won the role after two auditions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-NYT032615-10) She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in [season four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_4) "Mad Men (season 4)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Kiddieland-5)

As part of _Mad Men_'s ensemble cast, she won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series") in 2008 and 2009.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-11) Shipka received praise for her performance on _Mad Men_. In 2010, _[Austin American-Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin\_American-Statesman "Austin American-Statesman")_ critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actress_in_a_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series"), writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming _Mad Men_ work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in [season three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Men_(season_3) "Mad Men (season 3)"), this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-roe-12)

Beginning in 2012, Shipka voiced [Jinora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender_characters#Jinora "List of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters") in the [Nickelodeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon "Nickelodeon") animated series _[The Legend of Korra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Korra "The Legend of Korra")_, the sequel to _[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:\_The\_Last\_Airbender "Avatar: The Last Airbender")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-castinitial-13) In 2014, Shipka was named one of "The 25 Most Influential Teens of 2014" by [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Magazine "Time Magazine").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-14) That same year, [IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire") included her in their list of "20 Actors To Watch That Are Under 20".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-15) She starred in the 2014 [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") movie _[Flowers in the Attic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers\_in\_the\_Attic\_(2014\_film) "Flowers in the Attic (2014 film)")_, based on the [1979 novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_in_the_Attic "Flowers in the Attic") by [V. C. Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._C._Andrews "V. C. Andrews").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-16) The following year she co-starred with [Emma Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Roberts "Emma Roberts") in the [Osgood Perkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_Perkins "Oz Perkins") horror film _[The Blackcoat's Daughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blackcoat's\_Daughter "The Blackcoat's Daughter")_, and with [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet") in the fantasy thriller _[One & Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_&\_Two "One & Two")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-18) Additionally, she voiced the title character in the English dub of [Studio Ghibli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli "Studio Ghibli")'s _[When Marnie Was There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_Marnie\_Was\_There\_(film) "When Marnie Was There (film)")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-19) In 2017, Shipka portrayed [B.D. Hyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.D._Hyman "B.D. Hyman"), daughter of [Bette Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bette_Davis "Bette Davis"), in the [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") television series _[Feud: Bette and Joan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud\_(American\_TV\_series) "Feud (American TV series)")_.

### 2018–2021: _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Chilling Adventures of Sabrina")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png/250px-Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kiernan_Shipka_in_2018_-_1.png)

Shipka in 2018.

In January 2018, Shipka was announced to be starring as [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") in [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina\_(TV\_series) "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)")_ series based on the [comic series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-deadline-3) The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-20) and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-21) Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_, "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-23)

Shipka played a deaf teenager opposite [Stanley Tucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Tucci "Stanley Tucci") in [John R. Leonetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Leonetti "John R. Leonetti")'s [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(2019\_film) "The Silence (2019 film)")_, based on the 2015 novel of the same name by [Tim Lebbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Lebbon "Tim Lebbon").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-24) Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-25) Shipka learned [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. It's been spellbinding watching her."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-26) That same year, Shipka co-starred in the [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_film "Christmas film")[romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") film _[Let It Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow\_(2019\_film) "Let It Snow (2019 film)")_, based on the novel _[Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_It\_Snow:\_Three\_Holiday\_Romances "Let It Snow: Three Holiday Romances")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-27)

### 2022–present: Further work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2022–present: Further work")]

In 2022, Shipka starred alongside [Diane Kruger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Kruger "Diane Kruger") in the psychological drama series _[Swimming with Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming\_with\_Sharks\_(TV\_series) "Swimming with Sharks (TV series)")_, inspired by the [1994 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_with_Sharks "Swimming with Sharks").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-28) She also played Bea Johnson, the daughter of two intellectually disabled parents, in the drama _[Wildflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildflower\_(2022\_film) "Wildflower (2022 film)")_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-30) The following year she appeared in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") political drama limited series [_White House Plumbers_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Plumbers_(miniseries) "White House Plumbers (miniseries)"), portraying Kevan Hunt, daughter of [E. Howard Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._Howard_Hunt "E. Howard Hunt").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-31) In October 2023, Shipka starred alongside actress [Olivia Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Holt "Olivia Holt") in [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video")'s 1980s horror-comedy _[Totally Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totally\_Killer "Totally Killer")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Hollywood_Reporter-32)

In July 2024, Shipka appeared in the horror thriller _[Longlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longlegs "Longlegs")_, reuniting her with _The Blackcoat's Daughter_ director Osgood Perkins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-33) Later that year, she had supporting roles in the films _[Twisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisters\_(film) "Twisters (film)")_, _[The Last Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Showgirl "The Last Showgirl")_ and _[Red One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_One\_(film) "Red One (film)")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-36) In addition, she co-starred alongside [Nico Hiraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Hiraga "Nico Hiraga") in the [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") romantic comedy _[Sweethearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweethearts\_(2024\_film) "Sweethearts (2024 film)")_,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-37) and in the thriller film _[Stone Cold Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone\_Cold\_Fox "Stone Cold Fox")_, which premiered in November 2025.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-38)

In 2026, she appeared in the fourth season of the HBO/[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") drama _[Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry\_(TV\_series) "Industry (TV series)")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-Shipka,_Farthing,_Jimoh,_and_James-Kelly-39) She also starred in the comedy film _[Idiots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiots\_(2026\_film) "Idiots (2026 film)")_, which premiered at the [2026 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Sundance_Film_Festival "2026 Sundance Film Festival").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-41)

She is set to star alongside [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") in the romantic comedy _[Goodbye Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye\_Girl\_(film) "Goodbye Girl (film)")_,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-42) as well as _The Nowhere Game_, which will reunite her with [Mckenna Grace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mckenna_Grace "Mckenna Grace"), who portrayed the younger version of her character in _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kiernan_Shipka&oldid=1375648144#cite_note-43)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Riverdale (season 6)](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(season_6)&redirect=no "Riverdale (season 6)"))

_[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_ is an American [teen drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama") television series based on the characters of [Archie Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics"). The series was adapted for [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") by Archie Comics' chief creative officer [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa"), and is produced by [Warner Bros. Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Television "Warner Bros. Television") and [CBS Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Studios "CBS Studios"), in association with [Berlanti Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlanti_Productions "Berlanti Productions") and Archie Comics. Originally conceived as a feature film adaptation for [Warner Bros. Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Pictures "Warner Bros. Pictures"), the idea was re-imagined as a television series for [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company"). In 2015, development on the project moved to The CW, where the series was ordered for a pilot. Filming takes place in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"). The series debuted on January 26, 2017.

It features an ensemble cast based on the [characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Archie_Comics_characters "List of Archie Comics characters") of Archie Comics, with [KJ Apa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KJ_Apa "KJ Apa") in the role of [Archie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews "Archie Andrews"); [Lili Reinhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lili_Reinhart "Lili Reinhart") as [Betty Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Cooper "Betty Cooper"), [Camila Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Mendes "Camila Mendes") as [Veronica Lodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Lodge "Veronica Lodge"), [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") as [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones"), the series' narrator, [Madelaine Petsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelaine_Petsch "Madelaine Petsch") as [Cheryl Blossom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom"), [Ashleigh Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashleigh_Murray "Ashleigh Murray") as [Josie McCoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josie_McCoy "Josie McCoy"), [Vanessa Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Morgan "Vanessa Morgan") as [Toni Topaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Topaz "Toni Topaz"), [Charles Melton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Melton_(actor) "Charles Melton (actor)") as [Reggie Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Mantle "Reggie Mantle") and [Casey Cott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Cott "Casey Cott") as [Kevin Keller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Keller_(comics) "Kevin Keller (comics)"). During the course of the series, 137 episodes of _Riverdale_ aired over seven seasons, between January 26, 2017, and August 23, 2023.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Riverdale (season 6)](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(season_6)&redirect=no "Riverdale (season 6)"))

_[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_ is an American [teen drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama") television series based on the characters of [Archie Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics"). The series was adapted for [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") by Archie Comics' chief creative officer [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa"), and is produced by [Warner Bros. Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Television "Warner Bros. Television") and [CBS Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Studios "CBS Studios"), in association with [Berlanti Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlanti_Productions "Berlanti Productions") and Archie Comics. Originally conceived as a feature film adaptation for [Warner Bros. Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Pictures "Warner Bros. Pictures"), the idea was re-imagined as a television series for [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company"). In 2015, development on the project moved to The CW, where the series was ordered for a pilot. Filming takes place in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"). The series debuted on January 26, 2017.

It features an ensemble cast based on the [characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Archie_Comics_characters "List of Archie Comics characters") of Archie Comics, with [KJ Apa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KJ_Apa "KJ Apa") in the role of [Archie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews "Archie Andrews"); [Lili Reinhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lili_Reinhart "Lili Reinhart") as [Betty Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Cooper "Betty Cooper"), [Camila Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Mendes "Camila Mendes") as [Veronica Lodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Lodge "Veronica Lodge"), [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") as [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones"), the series' narrator, [Madelaine Petsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelaine_Petsch "Madelaine Petsch") as [Cheryl Blossom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom"), [Ashleigh Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashleigh_Murray "Ashleigh Murray") as [Josie McCoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josie_McCoy "Josie McCoy"), [Vanessa Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Morgan "Vanessa Morgan") as [Toni Topaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Topaz "Toni Topaz"), [Charles Melton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Melton_(actor) "Charles Melton (actor)") as [Reggie Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Mantle "Reggie Mantle") and [Casey Cott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Cott "Casey Cott") as [Kevin Keller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Keller_(comics) "Kevin Keller (comics)"). During the course of the series, 137 episodes of _Riverdale_ aired over seven seasons, between January 26, 2017, and August 23, 2023.
