_**Chilling Adventures of Sabrina**_ is an American [supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural_fiction "Supernatural fiction")[horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_fiction "Horror fiction") television series developed by [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa") for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), based on the [Archie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics")[comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book")[series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina"). It ran from October 2018 to December 2020 for two seasons (split in four parts). The series is produced by [Warner Bros. Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Television "Warner Bros. Television"), in association with [Berlanti Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlanti_Productions "Berlanti Productions") and Archie Comics. Aguirre-Sacasa and [Greg Berlanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Berlanti "Greg Berlanti") serve as executive producers, alongside [Sarah Schechter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Schechter_(producer) "Sarah Schechter (producer)"), Jon Goldwater, and [Lee Toland Krieger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Toland_Krieger "Lee Toland Krieger").

The series is centered on the [Archie Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics") character [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman"), portrayed by Kiernan Shipka, and also stars [Ross Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Lynch "Ross Lynch"), [Lucy Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Davis "Lucy Davis"), [Miranda Otto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Otto "Miranda Otto"), [Chance Perdomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chance_Perdomo "Chance Perdomo"), [Michelle Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Gomez "Michelle Gomez"), [Jaz Sinclair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaz_Sinclair "Jaz Sinclair"), [Tati Gabrielle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tati_Gabrielle "Tati Gabrielle"), [Adeline Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adeline_Rudolph "Adeline Rudolph"), [Lachlan Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lachlan_Watson "Lachlan Watson"), [Gavin Leatherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin_Leatherwood "Gavin Leatherwood"), and [Richard Coyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Coyle "Richard Coyle"). Originally in development during September 2017 at [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW"), the series was intended to be a companion series to _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_; however, in December 2017, the project was moved to Netflix with a straight-to-series order, consisting of twenty episodes. Filming took place in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia").

The first half of the first season, consisting of ten episodes, was released on October 26, 2018. The series received positive reviews, with critics praising Shipka's performance, as well as the premise, visuals, and directing. A [Christmas special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_special "Christmas special") episode was released on December 14, 2018, and the second half of the first season was released on April 5, 2019, consisting of nine episodes. In December 2018, Netflix renewed the series for a second season consisting of 16 episodes, split into two equal parts, of which the first eight episodes were released on January 24, 2020, with the second set released on December 31, 2020.

In July 2020, Netflix cancelled the series due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). Two [crossovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_(fiction) "Crossover (fiction)") with _Riverdale_ occurred during the [sixth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_season_6 "Riverdale season 6") of the latter series, acting as a backdoor series finale, with Shipka reprising her role. A comic book series continuation, titled _The Occult World of Sabrina_, was also announced.

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

_Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ is set in the fictional town of Greendale. It is a dark coming-of-age story that includes horror, fear and [witchcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft "Witchcraft"). [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") must reconcile her dual nature as a half-witch, half-mortal while fighting the evil forces that threaten her, her family, and the daylight world humans inhabit.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Shipka-1)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Development")]

In September 2017, it was reported that a live-action television series based on the comic book _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina")_ was being developed for [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") by [Warner Bros. Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Television "Warner Bros. Television") and [Berlanti Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlanti_Productions "Berlanti Productions"), with a planned release in the 2018–19 television season. The series would be a companion series to _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_. [Lee Toland Krieger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Toland_Krieger "Lee Toland Krieger") would direct the pilot, which would be written by [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa"). Both are executive producers along with [Greg Berlanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Berlanti "Greg Berlanti"), [Sarah Schechter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Schechter_(producer) "Sarah Schechter (producer)"), and Jon Goldwater.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeriesAnnounce-12) In December 2017, the project had moved to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") under a yet-to-be-announced new title. Two seasons, comprising ten episodes each, had been ordered by the streaming service;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) this was later altered to be one, 20-episode season split across two parts.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoVariety-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoTVLine-15) CW President Mark Pedowitz stated that Netflix's ability to offer a two-season commitment enticed Warner Bros. Television to move the series to the streaming service.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-PedowtizJan2018-16) In early May 2018, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ was officially confirmed as the series' title.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-TitleConfirm-17) The series was inspired by "slow-burn horror" films such as _[The Exorcist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Exorcist "The Exorcist")_, _[Rosemary's Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary's\_Baby\_(film) "Rosemary's Baby (film)")_, and other "great satanic horror movies from the 1960s and 1970s".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-EWSep2018-18) The opening title sequence features the art of Robert Hack, the original artist of the comic book series.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-19)

On November 12, 2018, Netflix announced that the eleventh episode of the twenty episodes ordered would be released as a [Christmas special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_special "Christmas special") episode.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-HolidaySpecial-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Special11thEpisode-21) It was not always the plan for the series to have a Christmas-themed episode. During production of the first episode of the second part, Aguirre-Sacasa realized that the series had already done episodes related to Halloween and Thanksgiving in the first part, and decided to create the episode. He noted the episode "was by and large self-contained, but that there are still elements that carry it through and the realizations and relationships and mythology — it sort of threads the needle. And so we figured out a story that could do both." The episode was also helpful for Netflix, who wanted some sort of additional, standalone content to release between the first two parts.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-ChristmasSpecialWrap-22) On December 18, 2018, Netflix renewed the series for a second season of 16 episodes, which was also split into two parts.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoVariety-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoTVLine-15) On July 8, 2020, Netflix cancelled the series due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-24)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Filming")]

Filming for the first part began on March 19, 2018, just as filming of the second season of _Riverdale_ concluded, which allowed the same crew members to work on both series.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-32) The first two parts were filmed back-to-back,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-THRFilming-33) with filming on the second part concluding on December 21, 2018.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-34) Filming had been expected to begin in February 2018 and last until June 2018.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-THRFilming-33) The first episode of the second part was the eleventh episode filmed, while the Christmas special was the twelfth episode filmed, despite the Christmas special being released as the eleventh episode overall in the series. This was because the idea for the Christmas special came about when the first episode of the second part was "too far down the line" to alter its production schedule. Despite the production switch, Aguirre-Sacasa said the first episode of the second part was written "as a premiere episode for the second part" and helps kick-off the storylines for the part.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-ChristmasSpecialWrap-22) Production on the second season, consisting of the third and fourth parts, began on May 17, 2019, and concluded on February 22, 2020.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2ProductionDates-35)

### Connection to _Riverdale_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Connection to Riverdale")]

The series was originally conceived as a companion series to _Riverdale_ when it was in development for the CW; however, after the series was moved to Netflix, it was unclear if any connection would remain. In January 2018, CW president Mark Pedowitz noted that, "at the moment, there is no discussion about crossing over."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-PedowtizJan2018-16) In March 2018, Jon Goldwater confirmed that the two series were "two separate entities for right now" but "would love it if they could figure out a way to cross over." Goldwater also felt there was a possibility for the characters to appear on future episodes of _Riverdale_, since Greendale had already been mentioned as existing on that series.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-36)

Sabrina's town, Greendale, is introduced in the second season of _Riverdale_. Following that, several references to the two cities are made regularly in the two series, visually or in dialogue.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-37) In the first season of _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_, Moses Thiessen reprises his role as Ben Button from _Riverdale_ during an episode.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-38) In the episode "Chapter Sixty-Seven: Varsity Blues" from the fourth season of _Riverdale_, [Ty Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Wood "Ty Wood") reprises his role as Billy Marlin from _Sabrina_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-39)

In episode "Chapter Twenty-Three: Heavy Is the Crown" from the third part of _Sabrina_, the teenage witch and her cousin visit Riverdale in search for a crown that was owned by Benjamin Blossom, an ancestor of [Cheryl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom"). On their way, they pass the town sign. On its back, [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones") spray painted the message "JJ Wuz Here", his signature. Three episodes later, a member of the Southside Serpents is attacked by a mutated Hilda Spellman.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-40)

In episode "Chapter Thirty-Four: The Returned" from the fourth part of _Sabrina_, a battle-of-the-bands poster lists the "Fred Heads" as an entrant in the competition. This was the name of the high school garage band of [Archie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews "Archie Andrews")'s father Fred Andrews.

Regarding a proper crossover, Aguirre-Sacasa said in October 2018 he would "hate [for a crossover] to never happen" between the two series, adding that a potential idea for one would see the characters of _Riverdale_ "hear[ing] about a haunted house in Greendale and try[ing] to break in and it's Sabrina's house". He also stated that since both series were already established, a crossover could happen in a standalone film with both casts, potentially titled _Afterlife with Archie_, based on the [Archie Horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Horror "Archie Horror") comic book series of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afterlife_with_Archie "Afterlife with Archie").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-41)

On October 7, 2021, it was announced that Shipka would be reprising her role as Sabrina in the sixth season of _Riverdale_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-42) During the same season, the series introduced the character Heather Chandler, played by Caroline Day, a witch from Greendale and from Sabrina's coven.

### Lawsuit

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Lawsuit")]

In November 2018, [Satanic Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satanic_Temple "Satanic Temple") activists sued the series' production team over the use of the [Statue of _Baphomet_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Baphomet "Statue of Baphomet"), which they claim was a direct copy of their own statue and portrayed the Temple in an inaccurate and derogatory way.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-bbc46147144-45) Temple members were also concerned about the depiction of Satanists as cannibals practicing forced worship.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-bbc46147144-45) On November 21, 2018, it was confirmed that Satanic Temple and Netflix had amicably settled the lawsuit dispute, with the terms of the deal left undisclosed to the public.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-46)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Release")]

The first ten episodes of _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ were released worldwide on Netflix on October 26, 2018.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S1ReleaseDate-54) The same day, the first two episodes were shown in a special screening at [Paris Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic-Con_Paris "Comic-Con Paris") 2018.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Paris-55) The eleventh episode of the first part, a [Christmas special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_special "Christmas special") episode, was released on December 14, 2018.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-HolidaySpecial-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Special11thEpisode-21) The remaining nine episodes of the first season were released on April 5, 2019.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Part2Release-56)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Special11thEpisode-21) The first part of the second season, dubbed Part 3, was released on January 24, 2020.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Season2January-57) The second part of the second season, also the last part of the series, dubbed Part 4, released on December 31, 2020.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Part4Release1-58)

#### Part 1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Part 1")]

For the first part of the first season, the review aggregator website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") reported a 91% approval rating with an average rating of 7.77/10 based on 103 reviews. The website's consensus reads, "Bewitchingly beautiful and wickedly macabre, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ casts an intoxicating spell and provides a perfect showcase for Kiernan Shipka's magical talents."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S1RT-59)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 74 out of 100 based on 28 critics for the first part of the first season, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S1MC-60)

Alicia Lutes of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ gave Part 1 a 9.2/10, saying that it "shines in its deliciously dark plotlines, volumes of camp, and irreverent and at-times antagonistic humor."[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-64) Dave Nemetz of [TVLine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVLine "TVLine") gave Part 1 a "B+" saying that "_Sabrina_ is more tongue-in-cheek and self-aware than _Riverdale_ is ever allowed to be" and that it is "off to a bewitchingly great start."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-65) Meagan Navarro from [Bloody Disgusting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloody_Disgusting "Bloody Disgusting") praised Part 1, stating that it is "fun and briskly paced".[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-66)

Daniel Fienberg from _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ stated in a review of Part 1, that the "appeal of Sabrina, increasing as the show goes along, comes mostly from Shipka". He praises the actress's performance by mentioning that she is "perfectly cast complement to one of the show's most endearing elements, namely its blurry approach to modernity."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-67) Chris Hayner from _[GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot")_ praised Part 1 by highlighting the performances of the cast members. He further complimented the progressive undertones of the series and stated that it "manages to tangle with modern day issues many face, while couching it all in a supernatural world".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-68) Constance Grady from _[Vox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox\_(website) "Vox (website)")_ praised Part 1, particularly for its cinematography, stating that its "higher production values are apparent in every frame, and the result is gorgeous". She further added that when the series fully commits to its dark goth horror aesthetic, it is at "its most thrilling."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-69) Petrana Radulovic from _[Polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon\_(website) "Polygon (website)")_ stated in her positive review of Part 1 that "once the horror kicks in, the season continues with just as much chills and sets the stage for what comes next."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-70)

For the Christmas special episode, Rotten Tomatoes reported a 76% approval rating with an average rating of 6.56/10 based on 21 reviews. The website's consensus reads, "This holiday chapter from Sabrina's _Chilling Adventures_ spikes the eggnog with the series' ghoulish sensibility, but viewers may feel disappointed by the special's confusion over whether it is a self-contained diversion or a continuation of the series' core story."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-71)

The seventh episode of the first season is particularly controversial for its depiction of a teenage orgy.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-73)

#### Part 2

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Part 2")]

The second part of the first season received an average of 6.88 out of 10 on Rotten Tomatoes, with an overall 81% approval based on 43 reviews. The website's consensus reads, "With a stronger mystery steeped in witchy world-building, _Chilling Adventures_ remains a deliciously dark, delightfully campy romp that pushes Sabrina deeper down the path of night — if only she would get there a little faster."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2RT-61)

#### Part 3

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Part 3")]

Rotten Tomatoes reports that 90% of 29 critic ratings are positive for the Part 3, with an average rating of 7.36/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "A deliciously hellish thrill ride from start to finish, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ just keeps getting better."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S3RT-62)

#### Part 4

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Part 4")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, Part 4 has an approval rating of 67% based on reviews from 24 critics, with an average rating of 7.13/10. The website's critical consensus states, "Though it leaves some fan favorites high and dry, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_'s final season hits enough emotional highs to serve as a fitting farewell to the Queen of Hell."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S4RT-63)

## Future and continuation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Future and continuation")]

Following the series' cancellation, Kiernan Shipka reprised her role as Sabrina in the episode "[Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Riverdale_episodes#ep99 "List of Riverdale episodes")" from the sixth season of _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_. The episode is set in an alternative universe called Rivervale where Sabrina is called by [Cheryl Blossom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom") ([Madelaine Petsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelaine_Petsch "Madelaine Petsch")) to help her with a spell. Shipka also reprised the role in "[Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Riverdale_episodes#ep114 "List of Riverdale episodes")" during the same season, an episode set in the original continuity of the two series and after the events of _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_. The episode provides closure to plot points from the series.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SabrinaSix-84) Nicholas Scratch also appeared in the episode, portrayed by [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse"), following a temporary resurrection spell used on [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones")'s body.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-NickRiverdale-85)

In July 2021, it was announced that the prospective fifth part and third season would be published as the comic book sequel series _The Occult World of Sabrina_. The first arc of the series would finish the "World Without Sabrina" storyline that began at the end of the series finale.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-TOWOS-86)

Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa also announced that a comics [crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_(fiction) "Crossover (fiction)") with _Riverdale_ and another one with the [original comic book series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina") are also being considered.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-TOWOS-86)

_**Chilling Adventures of Sabrina**_ is an American [supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural_fiction "Supernatural fiction")[horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_fiction "Horror fiction") television series developed by [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa") for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), based on the [Archie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics")[comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book")[series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina"). It ran from October 2018 to December 2020 for two seasons (split in four parts). The series is produced by [Warner Bros. Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Television "Warner Bros. Television"), in association with [Berlanti Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlanti_Productions "Berlanti Productions") and Archie Comics. Aguirre-Sacasa and [Greg Berlanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Berlanti "Greg Berlanti") serve as executive producers, alongside [Sarah Schechter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Schechter_(producer) "Sarah Schechter (producer)"), Jon Goldwater, and [Lee Toland Krieger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Toland_Krieger "Lee Toland Krieger").

The series is centered on the [Archie Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics") character [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman"), portrayed by Kiernan Shipka, and also stars [Ross Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Lynch "Ross Lynch"), [Lucy Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Davis "Lucy Davis"), [Miranda Otto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Otto "Miranda Otto"), [Chance Perdomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chance_Perdomo "Chance Perdomo"), [Michelle Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Gomez "Michelle Gomez"), [Jaz Sinclair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaz_Sinclair "Jaz Sinclair"), [Tati Gabrielle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tati_Gabrielle "Tati Gabrielle"), [Adeline Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adeline_Rudolph "Adeline Rudolph"), [Lachlan Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lachlan_Watson "Lachlan Watson"), [Gavin Leatherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin_Leatherwood "Gavin Leatherwood"), and [Richard Coyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Coyle "Richard Coyle"). Originally in development during September 2017 at [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW"), the series was intended to be a companion series to _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_; however, in December 2017, the project was moved to Netflix with a straight-to-series order, consisting of twenty episodes. Filming took place in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia").

The first half of the first season, consisting of ten episodes, was released on October 26, 2018. The series received positive reviews, with critics praising Shipka's performance, as well as the premise, visuals, and directing. A [Christmas special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_special "Christmas special") episode was released on December 14, 2018, and the second half of the first season was released on April 5, 2019, consisting of nine episodes. In December 2018, Netflix renewed the series for a second season consisting of 16 episodes, split into two equal parts, of which the first eight episodes were released on January 24, 2020, with the second set released on December 31, 2020.

In July 2020, Netflix cancelled the series due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). Two [crossovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_(fiction) "Crossover (fiction)") with _Riverdale_ occurred during the [sixth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_season_6 "Riverdale season 6") of the latter series, acting as a backdoor series finale, with Shipka reprising her role. A comic book series continuation, titled _The Occult World of Sabrina_, was also announced.

## Premise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Premise")]

_Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ is set in the fictional town of Greendale. It is a dark coming-of-age story that includes horror, fear and [witchcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft "Witchcraft"). [Sabrina Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Spellman "Sabrina Spellman") must reconcile her dual nature as a half-witch, half-mortal while fighting the evil forces that threaten her, her family, and the daylight world humans inhabit.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Shipka-1)

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Development")]

In September 2017, it was reported that a live-action television series based on the comic book _[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling\_Adventures\_of\_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina")_ was being developed for [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") by [Warner Bros. Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Television "Warner Bros. Television") and [Berlanti Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlanti_Productions "Berlanti Productions"), with a planned release in the 2018–19 television season. The series would be a companion series to _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_. [Lee Toland Krieger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Toland_Krieger "Lee Toland Krieger") would direct the pilot, which would be written by [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa"). Both are executive producers along with [Greg Berlanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Berlanti "Greg Berlanti"), [Sarah Schechter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Schechter_(producer) "Sarah Schechter (producer)"), and Jon Goldwater.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeriesAnnounce-12) In December 2017, the project had moved to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") under a yet-to-be-announced new title. Two seasons, comprising ten episodes each, had been ordered by the streaming service;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-13) this was later altered to be one, 20-episode season split across two parts.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoVariety-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoTVLine-15) CW President Mark Pedowitz stated that Netflix's ability to offer a two-season commitment enticed Warner Bros. Television to move the series to the streaming service.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-PedowtizJan2018-16) In early May 2018, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ was officially confirmed as the series' title.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-TitleConfirm-17) The series was inspired by "slow-burn horror" films such as _[The Exorcist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Exorcist "The Exorcist")_, _[Rosemary's Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary's\_Baby\_(film) "Rosemary's Baby (film)")_, and other "great satanic horror movies from the 1960s and 1970s".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-EWSep2018-18) The opening title sequence features the art of Robert Hack, the original artist of the comic book series.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-19)

On November 12, 2018, Netflix announced that the eleventh episode of the twenty episodes ordered would be released as a [Christmas special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_special "Christmas special") episode.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-HolidaySpecial-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Special11thEpisode-21) It was not always the plan for the series to have a Christmas-themed episode. During production of the first episode of the second part, Aguirre-Sacasa realized that the series had already done episodes related to Halloween and Thanksgiving in the first part, and decided to create the episode. He noted the episode "was by and large self-contained, but that there are still elements that carry it through and the realizations and relationships and mythology — it sort of threads the needle. And so we figured out a story that could do both." The episode was also helpful for Netflix, who wanted some sort of additional, standalone content to release between the first two parts.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-ChristmasSpecialWrap-22) On December 18, 2018, Netflix renewed the series for a second season of 16 episodes, which was also split into two parts.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoVariety-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SeasonTwoTVLine-15) On July 8, 2020, Netflix cancelled the series due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Cancellation-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-24)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Filming")]

Filming for the first part began on March 19, 2018, just as filming of the second season of _Riverdale_ concluded, which allowed the same crew members to work on both series.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-32) The first two parts were filmed back-to-back,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-THRFilming-33) with filming on the second part concluding on December 21, 2018.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-34) Filming had been expected to begin in February 2018 and last until June 2018.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-THRFilming-33) The first episode of the second part was the eleventh episode filmed, while the Christmas special was the twelfth episode filmed, despite the Christmas special being released as the eleventh episode overall in the series. This was because the idea for the Christmas special came about when the first episode of the second part was "too far down the line" to alter its production schedule. Despite the production switch, Aguirre-Sacasa said the first episode of the second part was written "as a premiere episode for the second part" and helps kick-off the storylines for the part.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-ChristmasSpecialWrap-22) Production on the second season, consisting of the third and fourth parts, began on May 17, 2019, and concluded on February 22, 2020.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2ProductionDates-35)

### Connection to _Riverdale_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Connection to Riverdale")]

The series was originally conceived as a companion series to _Riverdale_ when it was in development for the CW; however, after the series was moved to Netflix, it was unclear if any connection would remain. In January 2018, CW president Mark Pedowitz noted that, "at the moment, there is no discussion about crossing over."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-PedowtizJan2018-16) In March 2018, Jon Goldwater confirmed that the two series were "two separate entities for right now" but "would love it if they could figure out a way to cross over." Goldwater also felt there was a possibility for the characters to appear on future episodes of _Riverdale_, since Greendale had already been mentioned as existing on that series.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-36)

Sabrina's town, Greendale, is introduced in the second season of _Riverdale_. Following that, several references to the two cities are made regularly in the two series, visually or in dialogue.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-37) In the first season of _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_, Moses Thiessen reprises his role as Ben Button from _Riverdale_ during an episode.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-38) In the episode "Chapter Sixty-Seven: Varsity Blues" from the fourth season of _Riverdale_, [Ty Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Wood "Ty Wood") reprises his role as Billy Marlin from _Sabrina_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-39)

In episode "Chapter Twenty-Three: Heavy Is the Crown" from the third part of _Sabrina_, the teenage witch and her cousin visit Riverdale in search for a crown that was owned by Benjamin Blossom, an ancestor of [Cheryl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom"). On their way, they pass the town sign. On its back, [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones") spray painted the message "JJ Wuz Here", his signature. Three episodes later, a member of the Southside Serpents is attacked by a mutated Hilda Spellman.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-40)

In episode "Chapter Thirty-Four: The Returned" from the fourth part of _Sabrina_, a battle-of-the-bands poster lists the "Fred Heads" as an entrant in the competition. This was the name of the high school garage band of [Archie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews "Archie Andrews")'s father Fred Andrews.

Regarding a proper crossover, Aguirre-Sacasa said in October 2018 he would "hate [for a crossover] to never happen" between the two series, adding that a potential idea for one would see the characters of _Riverdale_ "hear[ing] about a haunted house in Greendale and try[ing] to break in and it's Sabrina's house". He also stated that since both series were already established, a crossover could happen in a standalone film with both casts, potentially titled _Afterlife with Archie_, based on the [Archie Horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Horror "Archie Horror") comic book series of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afterlife_with_Archie "Afterlife with Archie").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-41)

On October 7, 2021, it was announced that Shipka would be reprising her role as Sabrina in the sixth season of _Riverdale_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-42) During the same season, the series introduced the character Heather Chandler, played by Caroline Day, a witch from Greendale and from Sabrina's coven.

### Lawsuit

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Lawsuit")]

In November 2018, [Satanic Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satanic_Temple "Satanic Temple") activists sued the series' production team over the use of the [Statue of _Baphomet_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Baphomet "Statue of Baphomet"), which they claim was a direct copy of their own statue and portrayed the Temple in an inaccurate and derogatory way.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-bbc46147144-45) Temple members were also concerned about the depiction of Satanists as cannibals practicing forced worship.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-bbc46147144-45) On November 21, 2018, it was confirmed that Satanic Temple and Netflix had amicably settled the lawsuit dispute, with the terms of the deal left undisclosed to the public.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-46)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Release")]

The first ten episodes of _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ were released worldwide on Netflix on October 26, 2018.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S1ReleaseDate-54) The same day, the first two episodes were shown in a special screening at [Paris Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic-Con_Paris "Comic-Con Paris") 2018.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Paris-55) The eleventh episode of the first part, a [Christmas special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_special "Christmas special") episode, was released on December 14, 2018.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-HolidaySpecial-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Special11thEpisode-21) The remaining nine episodes of the first season were released on April 5, 2019.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Part2Release-56)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Special11thEpisode-21) The first part of the second season, dubbed Part 3, was released on January 24, 2020.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Season2January-57) The second part of the second season, also the last part of the series, dubbed Part 4, released on December 31, 2020.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-Part4Release1-58)

#### Part 1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Part 1")]

For the first part of the first season, the review aggregator website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") reported a 91% approval rating with an average rating of 7.77/10 based on 103 reviews. The website's consensus reads, "Bewitchingly beautiful and wickedly macabre, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ casts an intoxicating spell and provides a perfect showcase for Kiernan Shipka's magical talents."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S1RT-59)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 74 out of 100 based on 28 critics for the first part of the first season, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S1MC-60)

Alicia Lutes of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ gave Part 1 a 9.2/10, saying that it "shines in its deliciously dark plotlines, volumes of camp, and irreverent and at-times antagonistic humor."[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-64) Dave Nemetz of [TVLine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVLine "TVLine") gave Part 1 a "B+" saying that "_Sabrina_ is more tongue-in-cheek and self-aware than _Riverdale_ is ever allowed to be" and that it is "off to a bewitchingly great start."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-65) Meagan Navarro from [Bloody Disgusting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloody_Disgusting "Bloody Disgusting") praised Part 1, stating that it is "fun and briskly paced".[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-66)

Daniel Fienberg from _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ stated in a review of Part 1, that the "appeal of Sabrina, increasing as the show goes along, comes mostly from Shipka". He praises the actress's performance by mentioning that she is "perfectly cast complement to one of the show's most endearing elements, namely its blurry approach to modernity."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-67) Chris Hayner from _[GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot")_ praised Part 1 by highlighting the performances of the cast members. He further complimented the progressive undertones of the series and stated that it "manages to tangle with modern day issues many face, while couching it all in a supernatural world".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-68) Constance Grady from _[Vox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox\_(website) "Vox (website)")_ praised Part 1, particularly for its cinematography, stating that its "higher production values are apparent in every frame, and the result is gorgeous". She further added that when the series fully commits to its dark goth horror aesthetic, it is at "its most thrilling."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-69) Petrana Radulovic from _[Polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon\_(website) "Polygon (website)")_ stated in her positive review of Part 1 that "once the horror kicks in, the season continues with just as much chills and sets the stage for what comes next."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-70)

For the Christmas special episode, Rotten Tomatoes reported a 76% approval rating with an average rating of 6.56/10 based on 21 reviews. The website's consensus reads, "This holiday chapter from Sabrina's _Chilling Adventures_ spikes the eggnog with the series' ghoulish sensibility, but viewers may feel disappointed by the special's confusion over whether it is a self-contained diversion or a continuation of the series' core story."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-71)

The seventh episode of the first season is particularly controversial for its depiction of a teenage orgy.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-73)

#### Part 2

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Part 2")]

The second part of the first season received an average of 6.88 out of 10 on Rotten Tomatoes, with an overall 81% approval based on 43 reviews. The website's consensus reads, "With a stronger mystery steeped in witchy world-building, _Chilling Adventures_ remains a deliciously dark, delightfully campy romp that pushes Sabrina deeper down the path of night — if only she would get there a little faster."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S2RT-61)

#### Part 3

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Part 3")]

Rotten Tomatoes reports that 90% of 29 critic ratings are positive for the Part 3, with an average rating of 7.36/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "A deliciously hellish thrill ride from start to finish, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_ just keeps getting better."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S3RT-62)

#### Part 4

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Part 4")]

On Rotten Tomatoes, Part 4 has an approval rating of 67% based on reviews from 24 critics, with an average rating of 7.13/10. The website's critical consensus states, "Though it leaves some fan favorites high and dry, _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_'s final season hits enough emotional highs to serve as a fitting farewell to the Queen of Hell."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-S4RT-63)

## Future and continuation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Future and continuation")]

Following the series' cancellation, Kiernan Shipka reprised her role as Sabrina in the episode "[Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Riverdale_episodes#ep99 "List of Riverdale episodes")" from the sixth season of _[Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale\_(American\_TV\_series) "Riverdale (American TV series)")_. The episode is set in an alternative universe called Rivervale where Sabrina is called by [Cheryl Blossom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom") ([Madelaine Petsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelaine_Petsch "Madelaine Petsch")) to help her with a spell. Shipka also reprised the role in "[Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Riverdale_episodes#ep114 "List of Riverdale episodes")" during the same season, an episode set in the original continuity of the two series and after the events of _Chilling Adventures of Sabrina_. The episode provides closure to plot points from the series.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-SabrinaSix-84) Nicholas Scratch also appeared in the episode, portrayed by [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse"), following a temporary resurrection spell used on [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones")'s body.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-NickRiverdale-85)

In July 2021, it was announced that the prospective fifth part and third season would be published as the comic book sequel series _The Occult World of Sabrina_. The first arc of the series would finish the "World Without Sabrina" storyline that began at the end of the series finale.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-TOWOS-86)

Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa also announced that a comics [crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_(fiction) "Crossover (fiction)") with _Riverdale_ and another one with the [original comic book series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina "Chilling Adventures of Sabrina") are also being considered.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilling_Adventures_of_Sabrina_(TV_series)#cite_note-TOWOS-86)

This is a **list of notable [child actors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_actor "Child actor") from the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States")**. These actors are aged 17 and under. When they turn 18, they legally become adults and are no longer listed as child actors but will be moved to the [list of former American child actors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_former_American_child_actors "List of former American child actors").

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_current_American_child_actors "Special:EditPage/List of current American child actors") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

*   the [Second Chechen War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Chechen_War "Second Chechen War") begins;
*   concern grows over the [Year 2000 problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Year_2000_problem "Year 2000 problem");
*   the [NATO bombing of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_bombing_of_Yugoslavia "NATO bombing of Yugoslavia") escalates the [Kosovo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_War "Kosovo War");

*   the [1999 Russian apartment bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Russian_apartment_bombings "1999 Russian apartment bombings") trigger a security crisis;
*   the [Kargil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kargil_War "Kargil War") erupts between [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") and [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan");
*   the [1999 Martha's Vineyard plane crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Martha's_Vineyard_plane_crash "1999 Martha's Vineyard plane crash") kills [John F. Kennedy Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Jr. "John F. Kennedy Jr.") and [Carolyn Bessette Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_Bessette_Kennedy "Carolyn Bessette Kennedy");
*   and [Pokémania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mania "Pokémania") sparks a global craze for [Pokemon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokemon "Pokemon").
