*   [KJ Apa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KJ_Apa "KJ Apa") as [Archie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews "Archie Andrews"): A former [high school football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school_football "High school football") player who has a passion for music. After graduating, he fought as an Army sergeant and is now a JROTC instructor at his old high school. He is deeply involved in protecting his community from any danger. He is childhood best friends with his next door neighbor, Betty Cooper, and best friends with Jughead Jones.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-jugheadJosie-3) He once dated Veronica Lodge in high school, but they broke up. He later begins a relationship with Betty, to whom he proposes in the season six finale. He also becomes invulnerable after surviving a bomb explosion. In season seven in the 1950s, he discovers a passion for poetry he settles down in Modesto, as a construction worker and amateur writer, where he meets a girl and starts a family with her. When he dies, he is buried in Riverdale next to his father.
*   [Lili Reinhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lili_Reinhart "Lili Reinhart") as [Betty Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Cooper "Betty Cooper"): A smart woman who is best friends with Archie, who she has a longtime crush on. She becomes friends with Veronica Lodge when she moves to town. In high school, she dates Jughead, with whom she runs the school paper. She breaks up with Jughead before going away to college. She becomes an FBI agent and operates from Riverdale. She gradually develops a relationship with Archie and becomes engaged to him in the season 6 finale. In the 1950s in season 7, after exploring her sexuality and finding her independence, she settles in New York, where she runs her own Women's magazine and adopts her daughter, Carla.
*   [Camila Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Mendes "Camila Mendes") as [Veronica Lodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Lodge "Veronica Lodge"): A former "[it girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_girl "It girl")" of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), she moves to Riverdale at the beginning of the series. She hopes to become a better person after reflecting on the turmoil in her life after her father is convicted and sent to prison. She is ambitious and wants to succeed, but also works to be humble and avoid trouble. She dates Archie and later Reggie in high school. In season five, she is revealed to have had an extremely successful career on Wall Street, which she had to give up because of a marriage to an abusive husband. Later she divorces and kills him. She briefly reunites with Archie but it ends quickly and she starts seeing Reggie again, though they eventually break up too. In season 6, she orders a hit on her father and later gains the power to generate poison. In the 1950s Veronica discovers a love for movies and after running the local theater, she moves to Hollywood, becomes a successful producer, and is even buried in the Hollywood Forever Cemetery after she dies.
*   [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") as [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones"): A philosophically inclined social outcast who is Archie's best friend[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-BettyJughead-4) and Betty's ex-boyfriend. He was the former leader of the Southside Serpents gang. He went on to become a published writer, English teacher, and an advisor at the Blue and Gold high school newspaper. He struggled with alcoholism but eventually got sober and started dating Tabitha Tate. In season 6, he developed the power to read minds and was key to defeating Percival Pickens. In the 1950s, he briefly dates Veronica while developing a passion for comic books, and goes on to create his company called Jughead's Mad House. Sprouse also portrays Narrator Jughead, who prevents the Riverdale and Rivervale timelines from merging.

She grew up in an abusive and controlling family all while dealing with the murder of her brother, Jason Blossom.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-7) She comes out as a lesbian in the second season,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-8) dates Toni throughout the rest of high school, until they broke up after graduation because of Toni's disapproving family.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-9) She forgoes college to stay in Riverdale and atone for her family's sins by turning their business around. In Season 6, she reconnects with her childhood crush Heather, who helps her develop her fire power and discover she's a witch, but they break up when Heather discovers Toni is Cheryl's soulmate. In season 7, she reunites with Toni in the 1950s, and they move to California, where they have a son named Dale. Reggie and Veronica break up in season 6 following the opening of their casino. In the season 6 finale he takes sole ownership of the casino. However, in Season 7, he only has eyes for Midge, getting her pregnant and trying to kickstart a music career to win her parents' approval to marry her. They marry and have a daughter, but he dies young just as his music career is starting to take off.
*   [Erinn Westbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erinn_Westbrook "Erinn Westbrook") as Tabitha Tate (seasons 5–7x01, special guest 7x08 onwards): Pop Tate's granddaughter, who moves to Riverdale to take over the family diner after Pop retires. She befriends Jughead and supports him on his sobriety journey, and they eventually begin dating. In season 6, she develops time travelling powers and learns she's Riverdale's Guardian Angel. She uses the last of her life and powers to send everyone back to the 1950s for the final season, while she tries to untangle and fix all the timelines. She returns to give everyone back their memories, but is unable to return them back to the present and cannot stay with them. Her 1950s counterpart moves back to Chicago, where she goes to business and law school, and becomes a civil rights advocate.

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(American_TV_series)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

[Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") began development on an _Archie_ feature film in 2013, after a pitch from writer Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and director [Jason Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Moore_(director) "Jason Moore (director)") that would have placed Archie's gang into a teen comedy feature film in the [John Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hughes_(filmmaker) "John Hughes (filmmaker)") tradition.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-RiverdalePodcast-30) The duo brought the project to Warner Bros., where a VP recommended a more [high-concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-concept "High-concept") direction involving [time travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel") or interdimensional portals, suggesting [Louis C. K.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_C._K. "Louis C. K.") to portray an older Archie.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-31)[Dan Lin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Lin "Dan Lin") and [Roy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Lee "Roy Lee") became producers on the project, which eventually stalled as priorities shifted at the studio towards larger [tentpole films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tent-pole_(entertainment) "Tent-pole (entertainment)"), and was reimagined as a television series.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-RiverdalePodcast-30) The series _Riverdale_ was in development at [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company"), with the network landing the project in 2014 with a [script deal plus penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Put_pilot "Put pilot").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-32) However, Fox did not go forward with the project. In 2015, the show's development was moved to [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-33) which officially ordered a pilot on January 29, 2016.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-34) On March 7, 2017, The CW announced that the series had been renewed for a second season.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Renewed-35) On April 2, 2018, The CW renewed the series for a third season, which premiered October 10, 2018.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Season3Premiere-main-36)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-37) On January 31, 2019, The CW renewed the series for a fourth season, that was planned to consist of 22 episodes.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-38)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-40) However, season four got shortened to 19 episodes instead because production was suspended on March 11, 2020, as a direct result of [the coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Canada "COVID-19 pandemic in Canada").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Petski-41) Only 19 of the 22 ordered episodes of the fourth season were completed before the [coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Ausiello-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Andreeva-43) The fourth season premiered on October 9, 2019.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-44)

"[Chapter Forty-Nine: Fire Walk with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Riverdale_episodes#ep49 "List of Riverdale episodes")" was the first to be dedicated to [Luke Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Perry "Luke Perry"), who died two days before the episode aired.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-45)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-46)

On January 7, 2020, the series was renewed for a fifth season, which began a year later on January 20, 2021.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-47)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2021SeasonStartDates-48)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-49)

On February 3, 2021, the series was renewed for a sixth season which was split into two parts, and it premiered on November 16, 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-50)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S6Premiere-51)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-52) On March 22, 2022, The CW renewed the series for a seventh season.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S7Renewal-53) On May 19, 2022, it was announced that the series will be concluding with its upcoming seventh season, which premiered on March 29, 2023. The series finale aired on August 23, 2023.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Final_season-54)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S7Premiere-55)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(American_TV_series)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

On February 9, 2016, [Lili Reinhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lili_Reinhart "Lili Reinhart") and [Cole Sprouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Sprouse "Cole Sprouse") were cast as [Betty Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Cooper "Betty Cooper") and [Jughead Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jughead_Jones "Jughead Jones"), respectively.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-56) Lili Reinhart almost did not land the role after her video-based audition, but after moving to LA and attending in-person casting, she managed to get chosen to play Betty Cooper.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-57) On February 24, 2016, [KJ Apa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KJ_Apa "KJ Apa") was cast as [Archie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Andrews "Archie Andrews") after a four-month worldwide talent search. Apa was one of the last to audition and landed the role just days later. Also that day, [Ashleigh Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashleigh_Murray "Ashleigh Murray") was cast as Josie McCoy, the lead singer for the popular band [Josie and the Pussycats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josie_and_the_Pussycats "Josie and the Pussycats"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-58) and [Luke Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Perry "Luke Perry") and [Madelaine Petsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelaine_Petsch "Madelaine Petsch") were also added as Fred Andrews, Archie's father, and [Cheryl Blossom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Blossom "Cheryl Blossom"), respectively.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-59)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-60) Two days later, [Camila Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Mendes "Camila Mendes") was cast as [Veronica Lodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Lodge "Veronica Lodge") marking her first acting role in a television show.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-61)

In March 2016, [Marisol Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marisol_Nichols "Marisol Nichols") and [Mädchen Amick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A4dchen_Amick "Mädchen Amick") joined the cast as Hermione Lodge and Alice Cooper, Veronica and Betty's mothers, respectively.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-63) A few days later, [Ross Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Butler_(actor) "Ross Butler (actor)"), Daniel Yang and Cody Kearsley were cast in the roles Reggie Mantle, Dilton Doiley and Moose Mason, respectively.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-64) The last actor to join the pilot was [Casey Cott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Cott "Casey Cott") as [Kevin Keller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Keller_(comics) "Kevin Keller (comics)"), the first openly gay character in [Archie Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Comics "Archie Comics") history.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-65)

In April 2017, [Mark Consuelos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Consuelos "Mark Consuelos") signed on for the second season to play Veronica Lodge's father, [Hiram Lodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiram_Lodge "Hiram Lodge").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-66) The role was in second position to his existing role on _[Pitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch\_(TV\_series) "Pitch (TV series)"),_ but the cancellation of that series was announced on May 1, 2017.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-67) The next month, [Charles Melton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Melton "Charles Melton") was cast to take over the role of Reggie from [Ross Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Butler_(actor) "Ross Butler (actor)") in season 2, due to his status as a series regular on _[13 Reasons Why](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13\_Reasons\_Why "13 Reasons Why")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Melton-20) Casey Cott, who played Kevin Keller, was promoted to a series regular.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-68) In July 2017, _[True Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Blood "True Blood")_ star [Brit Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Morgan "Brit Morgan") was cast in the recurring role of Penny Peabody, an attorney the Southside Serpents call in case of any run-ins with the law.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-69) In August 2017, [Graham Phillips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Phillips_(actor) "Graham Phillips (actor)") had been cast to play Nick St. Clair, Veronica's ex-boyfriend from New York.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-70)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-71)

In March 2018, [Andy Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Cohen_(television_personality) "Andy Cohen (television personality)") appeared in the [sixteenth episode of the second season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Riverdale_episodes#ep29 "List of Riverdale episodes") as himself. In the series, he and Hermione are friends. He previously offered her a role as a cast member on _[The Real Housewives of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Real\_Housewives\_of\_New\_York\_City "The Real Housewives of New York City")_; however, Hermione turned down the offer to keep things private for the Lodge family.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-72) In May 2018, Charles Melton and [Vanessa Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Morgan "Vanessa Morgan"), who play [Reggie Mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Mantle "Reggie Mantle") and Toni Topaz, respectively, would both be promoted to series regulars in the third season.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-MeltonMorgan-73) By the time of [New York Comic Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Comic_Con "New York Comic Con") 2018, [Gina Gershon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gina_Gershon "Gina Gershon") and [Trinity Likins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_Likins "Trinity Likins"), respectively, had been cast as Gladys Jones and Jellybean "J.B." Jones for the third season.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-74)

In November 2018, [Kelly Ripa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Ripa "Kelly Ripa"), the wife of Mark Consuelos, who portrays Hiram Lodge, was cast for a guest role as Hiram's mistress.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-75) Michael Consuelos, Kelly and Mark's son, was cast to make a guest appearance in a flashback episode as a younger Hiram.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-76) In October 2019, [Ryan Robbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Robbins "Ryan Robbins") was cast as Fred Andrews's older brother, Frank Andrews, who appeared during the fourth season.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-77)

On February 23, 2020, it was announced that both Ulrich and Nichols would be leaving the series.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-78)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-79) However, in June 2020, Nichols revealed that after having a long talk with showrunner Sacasa, she would be staying on for season five.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-80) In September 2020, it was announced that [Erinn Westbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erinn_Westbrook "Erinn Westbrook") would join the show as a new regular character named Tabitha Tate, the granddaughter of Pop Tate, who arrives in town to run her grandfather's malt shop and franchise from it.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ErinnW-81) In January 2021, Chris Mason was cast in a recurring role for the fifth season as Chad Gekko, Veronica's Wall Street husband.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-82) In December 2021, [Chris O'Shea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_O'Shea "Christopher O'Shea") joined the cast in a recurring role as Percival Pickens for the sixth season.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-83) In May 2022, Caroline Day joined the cast in a recurring role as Heather for the sixth season.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-84) On December 20, 2022, [Nicholas Barasch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Barasch "Nicholas Barasch") and Karl Walcott were cast in recurring capacities for the seventh season.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-85)

Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-86)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-87) Production on the remaining 12 episodes of season one began on September 7, 2016, in Vancouver.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-88) Sets included Pop Tate's Chock'lit [Fraser Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraser_Valley "Fraser Valley").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Fraser-90) The aerial view of Riverdale is Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilmore\_Girls "Gilmore Girls")_, and the landmark settings are the same used in both of the aforementioned series as well as in _[Hart of Dixie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hart\_of\_Dixie "Hart of Dixie")_.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-popbuzz-91) Filming for the second season started on June 22, 2017,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-92) and concluded on March 27, 2018.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-93) Filming for the third season started on July 6, 2018.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-94)

Filming for the fourth season began on July 8, 2019, and was originally expected to end on April 4, 2020.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-95) Production was suspended on March 11, 2020, as a direct result of the coronavirus pandemic, after a person working on the show came in contact with a person who tested positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Petski-41) Only nineteen of the twenty-two ordered episodes of the fourth season were completed.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Ausiello-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Andreeva-43) Series writer Brian E. Paterson later confirmed that they would shoot the remaining two episodes of season four when it was safe to do so.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-96) The fourth season ultimately concluded with episode nineteen. The remaining three episodes intended for the season were used for the start of the fifth season, before the series underwent a five-year time jump.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-97) Despite a later premiere, season five was not expected to have a shortened episode count.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-98)

Filming for the fifth season began on September 14, 2020.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-99) The following month, however, filming was suspended for a week due to COVID-19 testing delays.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-100)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-101) Production on season five wrapped-up on June 1, 2021.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-102) The sixth season commenced production on August 30, 2021, and concluded on June 16, 2022.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S6Filming-103) Filming for the seventh and final season began on October 17, 2022,[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-104) and concluded on June 25, 2023.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-105)

**Homages to other films and television shows**

Several reviewers have noted that the series' episode titles are often taken directly or slightly altered from the titles of older films.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-cmctv-106)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-pbuzz-107) For example, De Elizabeth of _[Teen Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen\_Vogue "Teen Vogue")_ points out that _Riverdale_'s pilot episode was named "River's Edge" after the 1986 [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River's_Edge "River's Edge"), and the season finale takes its name from 1997's _[The Sweet Hereafter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sweet\_Hereafter\_(film) "The Sweet Hereafter (film)")_.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-teenv-108) Executive producer Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa notes that this is a deliberate choice, in order to hint at what will happen in that episode.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-teenv-108) References to the fictional setting of the _[Black Mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mirror "Black Mirror")_ episode "[San Junipero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Junipero "San Junipero")" can be seen in season one as well as heard amongst dialogue in season two and three.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-109)

Additionally, Katie-Kouise Smith of Popbuzz notes that the opening credits for _Riverdale_ mirror those of the _[Twin Peaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin\_Peaks "Twin Peaks")_ television series, and are intended as an homage to that series' co-creator, [David Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lynch "David Lynch").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-popbuzz-91)

## Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(American_TV_series)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Music")]

Musical performances are featured throughout the series, a blend of cover versions and originals. Songs performed in episodes are released as digital singles after broadcast; [WaterTower Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WaterTower_Music "WaterTower Music") released a digital compilation for season 1 songs on May 12, 2017; season 2 on May 18, 2018; season 3 on May 17, 2019; season 4 on May 15, 2020; and season 5 on August 25, 2021.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-110)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-season_2_soundtrack-111)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-112)

An album of [Blake Neely](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Neely "Blake Neely")'s scoring for season 1 was released on compact disc by La-La Land Records, and simultaneously on download by WaterTower, on July 18, 2017.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-113) The season 2 album with scores from Neely and [Sherri Chung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherri_Chung "Sherri Chung") was released on CD by La-La Land on October 30, 2018[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-114) and on digital by WaterTower on November 16, 2018.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-season_2_score-115) A [Halloween episode score soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_Special_Halloween_Episode_(Original_Television_Score) "Riverdale Special Halloween Episode (Original Television Score)") was released on digital on October 31, 2019.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-116) The scoring for seasons 3 and 4 were released on separate digital albums on January 22, 2021.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-season_3-4_score-117)

WaterTower released the songs performed in the musical episodes on separate digital albums. The [_Carrie: The Musical_ soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale:_Special_Episode_%E2%80%93_Carrie:_The_Musical_(Original_Television_Soundtrack) "Riverdale: Special Episode – Carrie: The Musical (Original Television Soundtrack)") was released on April 19, 2018,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-118) followed by a vinyl edition released at [Urban Outfitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Outfitters "Urban Outfitters") stores on July 13.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-119) The [_Heathers: The Musical_ soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale:_Special_Episode_%E2%80%93_Heathers:_The_Musical_(Original_Television_Soundtrack) "Riverdale: Special Episode – Heathers: The Musical (Original Television Soundtrack)") was released March 21, 2019; the [_Hedwig and the Angry Inch_ soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale:_Special_Episode_%E2%80%93_Hedwig_and_the_Angry_Inch_the_Musical_(Original_Television_Soundtrack) "Riverdale: Special Episode – Hedwig and the Angry Inch the Musical (Original Television Soundtrack)") was released on April 15, 2020. The _Return of the Pussycats_ soundtrack, and the _Next to Normal_ soundtrack, were both released on September 8 and 30, 2021, respectively.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-120)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-123) The _American Psycho: The Musical_ soundtrack was released on June 12, 2022,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-124) and the _Archie the Musical_ soundtrack was released on July 5, 2023, respectively.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-125)

### Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(American_TV_series)&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Marketing")]

In July 2016, members of the cast and the executive producers attended San Diego Comic-Con to promote the upcoming series, where they premiered the first episode "Chapter One: The River's Edge".[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-148) The first trailer for the series was released in late December 2016.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-149) The CW also sponsored multiple [Tastemade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tastemade "Tastemade") videos, where they cooked several foods that are popular in the Archie universe.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-151)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-152)

### Tie-in media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Riverdale_(American_TV_series)&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Tie-in media")]

Along with heavily promoting the television series in their regular comics since January 2017, Archie Comics released a comic book adaptation of _Riverdale_, featuring auxiliary story arcs set within the television series' own [continuity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canon_(fiction) "Canon (fiction)"). The comic book adaptation is headed by [Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Aguirre-Sacasa "Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa") himself, along with other writers from the show. Alongside a one-shot pilot issue, illustrated by [Alitha Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alitha_Martinez "Alitha Martinez"), released in March 2017,[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-153) the first issue of the ongoing _Riverdale_ comic book series was released starting April 2017.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-AprilSolicits-154)

In addition to the adaptation, Archie Comics are releasing a series of compilation graphic novels branded under the title _Road to Riverdale_. This series features early issues from the _[New Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Riverdale "New Riverdale")_ reboot line, introducing the audience of the TV series to the regular ongoing comic series that inspired it. Archie Comics plans to re-print the volumes of _Road to Riverdale_ in subsequent months as [digest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digest_size "Digest size") magazines. The first volume was released in March 2017.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-AprilSolicits-154) Michol Ostow wrote a graphic novel _The Ties That Bind_, released in May 2021.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-155)

Several tie-in novels were also released in conjunction with the show, the first being _The Day Before_ a prequel novel set a day before the events of the first episode.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-156)_Get Out of Town_ is set between seasons 2 and 3,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and was followed by _The Maple Murders_, _Death of a Cheerleader_, and _The Poison Pen_. The first four novels were written by [Micol Ostow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micol_Ostow "Micol Ostow"), with the fifth book penned by Caleb Roehrig.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

gothic horror, fantasy, telenovelas, soap operas, comic books, gay art-house films, dark high-school comedies, musicals, and mafia movies and smushed them together into a pop-culture polycule—while the ensemble held it all together, putting it on like some sort of weekly vaudeville act."[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-vulture2023-168) Sam Bramesco of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ called it "a sprawling soap opera with a liberated relationship to reality, the finest specimen of its genre in its era" and an "unending parade of camp [that] never once committed the cardinal sin of being boring."[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-guardian-165) Emma Stefansky of _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ringer\_(website) "The Ringer (website)")_ opined that while some fans and journalists criticized subsequent seasons for "relying less and experience."[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ringer-166)

Critics have attributed the escalation to more absurd storytelling to the series' standard-length seasons of approximately 20 episodes, no longer the norm, especially for teen dramas, in the wake of television").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-guardian-165)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ringer-166)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-vulture2023-168)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-avclubend-169)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ew2023-170) Kristen Baldwin of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ opined that "the world where a network allows a lavish, sexy, teen genre drama to run off the rails for seven gloriously outlandish seasons no longer exists," and also noted that _Riverdale_ amid the CW's programming shift toward unscripted, sports, and acquired content under Group").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ew2023-170) Stefansky praised the CW for allowing a show such as _Riverdale_ to run for seven seasons while a of the series finale, Mary Kate Carr of _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_ stated that _Riverdale_ is the "dying gasp" of the teen drama of its era, as "streaming services have saturated the market so much that it's hard to imagine a new teen soap cultivating enough hype or strong enough fandom to command an entire hall at Comic-Con."[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-avclubend-169)

Many critics highlighted the show's deviation from its initial premise as a teen drama. In ranking the show's wildest storylines, Abby Monteil of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ noted that the series' initial high school-based plot "soon mutated beyond its teen-drama trappings, transforming from a _Twin Peaks_-esque reimagining of the comics' squeaky-clean source material into a campy, Frankensteinian mash-up of genres, pop-culture references, and pie-in-the-sky melodrama that's frankly unlike anything that came before it."[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-rollingstone-167) Stefansky noted that the series "never played by conventional teen television's rules; it poked fun at certain clichés while embracing others and mixed the strange with the familiar" and took "more inspiration from [Stephen King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King "Stephen King") and _Twin Peaks_ than from [John Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hughes_(filmmaker) "John Hughes (filmmaker)") or _[Gossip Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip\_Girl "Gossip Girl")_."[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ringer-166) Bramesco compared the series to [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_(filmmaker) "Ryan Murphy (filmmaker)")'s "similarly excessive, queer-inflected" _[American Horror Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Horror\_Story "American Horror Story")_, stating that while Murphy aims for prestige, Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa "staunchly refuses to take his work seriously, venturing deeper into his insular funhouse with the express purpose of getting lost."[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-guardian-165)

'''Kiernan Brennan Shipka''' (born November 10, 1999)<ref>{{cite news |last1=Todisco |first1=Eric |title=Jon Hamm Attends Mad Men Daughter Kiernan Shipka's 80th Birthday Bash: 'Dad Showed Up!' |url=https://people.com/tv/jon-hamm-attends-kiernan-shipka-20th-birthday/ |access-date=April 30, 2022 |work=People |date=November 11, 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="chicago tribune">{{cite web|last=Ryan|first=Maureen|title='Mad Men' star Kiernan Shipka takes drama in stride|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/ct-xpm-2010-08-13-ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813-story.html|website=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=April 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620161507/https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/ct-xpm-2010-08-13-ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813-story.html|archive-date=June 20, 2020 }}</ref> is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as [[List of Mad Men characters#Sally Draper|Sally Draper]] in the [[AMC (TV channel)|AMC]] drama series ''[[Mad Men]]'' (2007–2015), and [[Sabrina Spellman]] in the [[Netflix]] fantasy series ''[[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)|Chilling Adventures of Sabrina]]'' (2018–2020) and the sixth season of [[The CW]] series ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]'' (2021–2022).<ref name="deadline">{{cite web|last=Petski|first=Denise|title=Kiernan Shipka To Star In Netflix's Sabrina The Teenage Witch Series|url=https://deadline.com/2018/01/kiernan-shipka-star-netflix-sabrina-the-teenage-witch-series-1202236650|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=January 5, 2018 |access-date=January 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019032222/https://deadline.com/2018/01/kiernan-shipka-star-netflix-sabrina-the-teenage-witch-series-1202236650/ |archive-date=October 19, 2021 }}</ref>

In addition to supporting roles in films such as ''[[Longlegs]]'', ''[[Twisters (film)|Twisters]]'', and ''[[The Last Showgirl]]'' (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in ''[[The Blackcoat's Daughter]]'' (2015), ''[[Totally Killer]]'' (2023), and ''[[Sweethearts (2024 film)|Sweethearts]]'' (2024), among others.

==Early life==
Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in [[Chicago]], Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.<ref name=MadTween/><ref name=Kiddieland/><ref>{{cite web |title=Erin Brennan, John Shipka |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1995-12-23-9512230088-story.html |work=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US |date=December 23, 1995 |access-date=June 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319105521/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1995-12-23/entertainment/9512230088_1_chicago-erin-brennan-university-of-notre-dame |archive-date=March 19, 2013}}</ref> She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kiernan Shipka & Isabela Merced Answer the Web's Most Searched Questions |url=https://www.wired.com/video/watch/kiernan-shipka-isabela-merced-answer-the-web-s-most-searched-questions |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331092009/https://www.wired.com/video/watch/kiernan-shipka-isabela-merced-answer-the-web-s-most-searched-questions |archive-date=March 31, 2023 |url-status=live |work=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |language=en-US |date=November 9, 2019 |quote=Indeed I am, 62% Irish, hence the name Kiernan. Ay. My middle name is Brennan, which is also very Irish. Have a lot of Irish people in my family. My mom's name is Erin, also very Irish.|issn=1078-3148}}</ref> She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking [[ballroom dancing]] classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.<ref>{{cite news |last=Chang |first=Bee-Shyuan |date=March 23, 2012 |title=Growth Spurts Considered: Kiernan Shipka of 'Mad Men' — What I Wore |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/25/fashion/kiernan-shipka-of-mad-men.html |newspaper=The New York Times |language=en-US |access-date=September 21, 2012}}</ref> When she was six, her family relocated to [[Los Angeles]] to help with her acting career.<ref name=Kiddieland/>

==Career==
===2000–2017: Beginnings and ''Mad Men''===
[[File:Kiernan Shipka (cropped 2).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Shipka at the 2010 [[Screen Actors Guild Awards]]]]
In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]''.<ref name="dazeddigital">{{cite web |last1=Barlow |first1=Eve |date=February 9, 2016 |title=Kiernan Shipka: wide awake in dreamland |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/artsandculture/article/29598/1/kiernan-shipka-wide-awake-in-dreamland |work=[[Dazed]] |language=en-US |access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref> She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.<ref name=MadTween>{{cite web |last=Ryan |first=Maureen |date=August 13, 2012 |title='Mad' tween takes drama in stride |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/ct-xpm-2010-08-13-ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813-story.html |work=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319105525/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-08-13/features/ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813_1_sally-draper-mad-men-mad-men-s |archive-date=March 19, 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as [[List of Mad Men characters#Sally Draper|Sally Draper]], the daughter of main character [[Don Draper]], on the 2007–2015 TV series ''[[Mad Men]]''. She won the role after two auditions.<ref name = NYT032615>{{cite news |last=Galanes |first=Philip |date=March 26, 2015 |title=Growing Up on 'Mad Men': A Conversation With Matthew Weiner and Kiernan Shipka |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/03/29/fashion/growing-up-on-mad-men-a-conversation-with-matthew-weiner-and-kiernan-shipka.html |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |access-date=March 28, 2015}}</ref> She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in [[Mad Men (season 4)|season four]].<ref name=Kiddieland>{{cite web |last=Rackl |first=Lori |date=March 23, 2012 |title=Chicago girl goes from Kiddieland to Sterling Cooper |url=http://www.suntimes.com/entertainment/television/11428482-421/chicago-girl-goes-from-kiddieland-to-sterling-cooper.html |work=[[Chicago Sun Times]] |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319105537/http://www.suntimes.com/entertainment/television/11428482-421/chicago-girl-goes-from-kiddieland-to-sterling-cooper.html |archive-date=March 19, 2013}}</ref>

As part of ''Mad Men''{{'}}s ensemble cast, she won the [[Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series]] in 2008 and 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory?id=9647207 |title=Stars of TV and Film Mingle at SAG Awards  |publisher=ABC News |access-date= March 2, 2010|date= January 24, 2010|first= Anthony|last= McCartney}}</ref> Shipka received praise for her performance on ''Mad Men''. In 2010, ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]'' critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series]], writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming ''Mad Men'' work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in [[Mad Men (season 3)|season three]], this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."<ref name="roe">Dale Roe. "Devoted TV watchers name their dream Emmy winners", ''Austin American-Statesman'', July 4, 2010, page H-1.</ref>

===2018–2021: ''Chilling Adventures of Sabrina''===
[[File:Kiernan Shipka in 2018 - 1.png|thumb|upright|Shipka in 2018.]]
In January 2018,  Shipka was announced to be starring as [[Sabrina Spellman]] in [[Netflix]]'s ''[[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)|Chilling Adventures of Sabrina]]'' series based on the [[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina|comic series of the same name]].<ref name="deadline" /> The first part was released by Netflix on October 26, 2018,<ref>{{cite web |last=Lutes |first=Alicia |date=October 26, 2018 |title=Netflix's Chilling Adventures of Sabrina: Season 1 Review |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/10/26/netflixs-chilling-adventures-of-sabrina-season-1-review |work=IGN |language=en-US |access-date= October 27, 2018 }}</ref> and an episode that December. The show ran for three more parts, concluding on December 31, 2020, with a total of 36 episodes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldstein |first1=Jessica |date=January 2, 2021 |title=Chilling Adventures of Sabrina Series Finale Recap: Enter the Void |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/chilling-adventures-of-sabrina-series-finale-recap-season-4-part-4-episode-8-at-the-mountains-of-madness.html |website=Vulture |language=en-US |access-date=November 30, 2021}}</ref> Shipka reprised the role in two episodes of ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]'', "Chapter Ninety-Nine: The Witching Hour(s)" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen: The Witches of Riverdale", which aired on December 7, 2021, and July 10, 2022, respectively.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mizoguchi |first1=Karen |date=November 30, 2021 |title=Kiernan Shipka on Riverdale! Leonetti]]'s [[horror film]] ''[[The Silence (2019 film)|The Silence]]'', based on the 2015 novel of the same name by [[Tim Lebbon]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Lodderhose |first=Diana |date=May 12, 2017 |title=Kiernan Shipka To Star In John Leonetti's 'The Silence' From Constantin Film & EMJAG – Cannes |url=https://deadline.com/2017/05/kiernan-shipka-john-leonetti-horror-the-silence-constantin-film-resident-evil-emjag-cannes-mister-smith-entertainment-1202091581/ |work=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> Netflix released the film on April 10, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last=Keveney |first=Bill |date=March 19, 2019 |title=New on Netflix in April 2019: Kevin Hart, 'Sabrina' and more Noah Centineo |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2019/03/19/netflix-april-highlights-include-kevin-hart-special-and-sabrina/3203491002/ |website=USA Today |language=en-US |access-date=February 2, 2026}}</ref> Shipka learned [[American Sign Language]] for the role and Leonetti praised her performance, saying: "She's acting alongside Stanley Tucci, and believe me, she's more than holding her own. '''Kiernan Brennan Shipka''' (born November 10, 1999)<ref>{{cite news |last1=Todisco |first1=Eric |title=Jon Hamm Attends Mad Men Daughter Kiernan Shipka's 80th Birthday Bash: 'Dad Showed Up!' |url=https://people.com/tv/jon-hamm-attends-kiernan-shipka-20th-birthday/ |access-date=April 30, 2022 |work=People |date=November 11, 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="chicago tribune">{{cite web|last=Ryan|first=Maureen|title='Mad Men' star Kiernan Shipka takes drama in stride|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/ct-xpm-2010-08-13-ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813-story.html|website=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=April 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620161507/https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/ct-xpm-2010-08-13-ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813-story.html|archive-date=June 20, 2020 }}</ref> is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as [[List of Mad Men characters#Sally Draper|Sally Draper]] in the [[AMC (TV channel)|AMC]] drama series ''[[Mad Men]]'' (2007–2015), and [[Sabrina Spellman]] in the [[Netflix]] fantasy series ''[[Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (TV series)|Chilling Adventures of Sabrina]]'' (2018–2020) and the sixth season of [[The CW]] series ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]'' (2021–2022).<ref name="deadline">{{cite web|last=Petski|first=Denise|title=Kiernan Shipka To Star In Netflix's Sabrina The Teenage Witch Series|url=https://deadline.com/2018/01/kiernan-shipka-star-netflix-sabrina-the-teenage-witch-series-1202236650|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=January 5, 2018 |access-date=January 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019032222/https://deadline.com/2018/01/kiernan-shipka-star-netflix-sabrina-the-teenage-witch-series-1202236650/ |archive-date=October 19, 2021 }}</ref>

In addition to supporting roles in films such as ''[[Longlegs]]'', ''[[Twisters (film)|Twisters]]'', and ''[[The Last Showgirl]]'' (all in 2024), Shipka has also had starring roles in ''[[The Blackcoat's Daughter]]'' (2015), ''[[Totally Killer]]'' (2023), and ''[[Sweethearts (2024 film)|Sweethearts]]'' (2024), among others.

==Early life==
Kiernan Brennan Shipka was born on November 10, 1999, in [[Chicago]], Illinois, to John Young Shipka, a real-estate developer, and Erin Ann Brennan.<ref name=MadTween/><ref name=Kiddieland/><ref>{{cite web |title=Erin Brennan, John Shipka |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1995-12-23-9512230088-story.html |work=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US |date=December 23, 1995 |access-date=June 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319105521/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1995-12-23/entertainment/9512230088_1_chicago-erin-brennan-university-of-notre-dame |archive-date=March 19, 2013}}</ref> She is of mostly Irish and Slovak descent.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kiernan Shipka & Isabela Merced Answer the Web's Most Searched Questions |url=https://www.wired.com/video/watch/kiernan-shipka-isabela-merced-answer-the-web-s-most-searched-questions |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331092009/https://www.wired.com/video/watch/kiernan-shipka-isabela-merced-answer-the-web-s-most-searched-questions |archive-date=March 31, 2023 |url-status=live |work=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |language=en-US |date=November 9, 2019 |quote=Indeed I am, 62% Irish, hence the name Kiernan. Ay. My middle name is Brennan, which is also very Irish. Have a lot of Irish people in my family. My mom's name is Erin, also very Irish.|issn=1078-3148}}</ref> She also has notable German, English, Scottish, and Italian heritage. Shipka started taking [[ballroom dancing]] classes at the age of five and was still attending classes as of March 2012.<ref>{{cite news |last=Chang |first=Bee-Shyuan |date=March 23, 2012 |title=Growth Spurts Considered: Kiernan Shipka of 'Mad Men' — What I Wore |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/25/fashion/kiernan-shipka-of-mad-men.html |newspaper=The New York Times |language=en-US |access-date=September 21, 2012}}</ref> When she was six, her family relocated to [[Los Angeles]] to help with her acting career.<ref name=Kiddieland/>

==Career==
===2000–2017: Beginnings and ''Mad Men''===
[[File:Kiernan Shipka (cropped 2).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Shipka at the 2010 [[Screen Actors Guild Awards]]]]
In April 2000, Shipka made her television debut at five months of age on the hospital drama ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]''.<ref name="dazeddigital">{{cite web |last1=Barlow |first1=Eve |date=February 9, 2016 |title=Kiernan Shipka: wide awake in dreamland |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/artsandculture/article/29598/1/kiernan-shipka-wide-awake-in-dreamland |work=[[Dazed]] |language=en-US |access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref> She started commercial-print modeling when she was a baby.<ref name=MadTween>{{cite web |last=Ryan |first=Maureen |date=August 13, 2012 |title='Mad' tween takes drama in stride |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/ct-xpm-2010-08-13-ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813-story.html |work=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319105525/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-08-13/features/ct-ae-0815-kiernan-shipka-20100813_1_sally-draper-mad-men-mad-men-s |archive-date=March 19, 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> After undertaking small television roles, her first major role was as [[List of Mad Men characters#Sally Draper|Sally Draper]], the daughter of main character [[Don Draper]], on the 2007–2015 TV series ''[[Mad Men]]''. She won the role after two auditions.<ref name = NYT032615>{{cite news |last=Galanes |first=Philip |date=March 26, 2015 |title=Growing Up on 'Mad Men': A Conversation With Matthew Weiner and Kiernan Shipka |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/03/29/fashion/growing-up-on-mad-men-a-conversation-with-matthew-weiner-and-kiernan-shipka.html |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |access-date=March 28, 2015}}</ref> She was a recurring guest star for the show's first three seasons, then became a series regular in [[Mad Men (season 4)|season four]].<ref name=Kiddieland>{{cite web |last=Rackl |first=Lori |date=March 23, 2012 |title=Chicago girl goes from Kiddieland to Sterling Cooper |url=http://www.suntimes.com/entertainment/television/11428482-421/chicago-girl-goes-from-kiddieland-to-sterling-cooper.html |work=[[Chicago Sun Times]] |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130319105537/http://www.suntimes.com/entertainment/television/11428482-421/chicago-girl-goes-from-kiddieland-to-sterling-cooper.html |archive-date=March 19, 2013}}</ref>

As part of ''Mad Men''{{'}}s ensemble cast, she won the [[Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series]] in 2008 and 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory?id=9647207 |title=Stars of TV and Film Mingle at SAG Awards  |publisher=ABC News |access-date= March 2, 2010|date= January 24, 2010|first= Anthony|last= McCartney}}</ref> Shipka received praise for her performance on ''Mad Men''. In 2010, ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]'' critic Dale Roe named her as his dream nominee for the [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series]], writing, "This 10-year-old actress was so affecting as troubled Sally Draper last season that it seems odd that she's only just been upgraded to series regular. If Shipka's upcoming ''Mad Men'' work—struggling with the broken marriage of her parents and entering preteendom in the tumultuous 1960s—remains as amazing as it was in [[Mad Men (season 3)|season three]], this is a ballot wish that could come true next year."<ref name="roe">Dale Roe. "Devoted TV watchers name their dream Emmy winners", ''Austin American-Statesman'', July 4, 2010, page H-1.</ref>

**Anonymous** most often refers to:

*   [Anonymity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymity "Anonymity"), the state of an individual's identity, or personally identifiable information, being publicly unknown 
    *   [Anonymous work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymous_work "Anonymous work"), a work of art or literature that has an unnamed or unknown creator or author

*   [Anonymity (social choice)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymity_(social_choice) "Anonymity (social choice)"), a property of a voting rule, saying that it does not discriminate apriori between voters
*   [Anonymous (hacker group)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymous_(hacker_group) "Anonymous (hacker group)"), the collective name of loosely affiliated individuals who participate in hacktivism
